name: U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz
status: Saudi Arabia's East-West 'Petroline' pipeline — the principal Hormuz-bypass route (~5M bpd to the Red Sea) — was struck by multiple drones launched from Iraqi territory on 10-11 Sep and shut down; satellite imagery published 14 Sep confirms the damage, upgrading the prior 'likely a known flare site' read to a confirmed attack with no claimed responsibility. The 14 Sep GCC-Iran Salalah, Oman ministerial meeting — the war's first multilateral dialogue — was postponed 'in the interest of consensus' after a fresh wave of attacks, including a 13 Sep strike near Qeshm Island (IRIB: 1 Iranian commercial-vessel crewmember killed, 4 injured) and a separate UKMTO-reported vessel hit by an unidentified projectile off Oman. Iran's AEOI head Mohammad Eslami was barred from traveling to the IAEA General Conference in Vienna after the US urged against a UN travel-ban waiver; Iran summoned the Austrian envoy in protest. A narrower Iran-Oman bilateral shipping-lane arrangement continues in parallel, and Abu Dhabi's Crown Prince met Iranian President Pezeshkian at the BRICS summit in New Delhi (13 Sep) — the first top-level Iran-UAE contact of the war. NSA Bahrain repair status unchanged (no return timeline).
importance: Critical — the Hormuz-bypass route and the leading multilateral diplomatic mechanism both failed within the same 72 hours, raising the sustained-risk floor for Gulf energy flows and shipping even without a single dramatic escalation.
assessment: A genuinely multi-track posture continues: deniable/unclaimed attacks on both shipping and now critical energy infrastructure run in parallel with multiplying (if so far unsuccessful or narrower) diplomatic channels — multilateral (stalled), bilateral Iran-Oman (continuing), and now Iran-UAE (newly opened). The Petroline attack's lack of claimed responsibility leaves attribution genuinely unresolved; the Salalah postponement is explicitly framed by Oman as temporary, not terminal.
lastChange: 2026-09-14 — Petroline pipeline attack confirmed via satellite imagery and pipeline closure; 14 Sep Salalah ministerial postponed; new Qeshm-area attacks (13 Sep); Eslami barred from IAEA Vienna conference; Iran-UAE leaders meet at BRICS (13 Sep).
orgRelevance: Reassess Gulf-transiting shipping, energy, and insurance exposure against a closed bypass pipeline and a stalled multilateral diplomatic mechanism — treat this as a sustained-disruption planning assumption, not an episodic crisis; watch for Petroline attribution/repair signals and any rescheduled meeting or bilateral shipping arrangement as the nearest inflections.
nextIndicator: Petroline attack attribution or Saudi repair-timeline announcement; a rescheduled Salalah meeting or an unveiled Iran-Oman bilateral shipping arrangement; further attacks during the diplomatic gap; any NSA Bahrain reconstruction-timeline announcement.

name: Critical Minerals / Rare-Earth Magnets
status: China's military-affiliated license-denial rule (since 1 Dec 2025) and the June 2026 entity-list targeting of MP Materials/USA Rare Earth remain the binding constraints; no new PRC action confirmed this cycle. The broader Oct 2025 rare-earth controls remain suspended until their 10 Nov 2026 expiry. Beijing has now formally confirmed Xi Jinping's 24 Sep 2026 Washington visit (agenda: trade, AI, the Iran war, Taiwan), giving this thread a concrete near-term inflection date.
importance: Critical — binding, targeted constraint on munitions/platform output and the domestic-substitution response itself, now with a confirmed summit date as the nearest potential inflection point ahead of the 10 Nov suspension-expiry decision.
assessment: Durable, weaponizable chokepoint at its already-escalated severity; no signal of near-term relaxation. The confirmed 24 Sep summit could move this constraint in either direction — easing via a trade gesture, or hardening if talks falter — making the pre- and post-summit window the key assessment period.
lastChange: 2026-09-14 — no new PRC action this cycle; Beijing formally confirms the 24 Sep Trump-Xi summit, establishing a concrete near-term watch date.
orgRelevance: Map magnet exposure in hardware BOMs against named entities; pursue second sources; treat the pre/post-summit window (through ~24-26 Sep) as a dedicated watch period for any licensing signal.
nextIndicator: Any rare-earth signal at or around the 24 Sep summit; DoD mine-to-magnet award cadence; any further PRC entity-list or licensing action; the 10 Nov 2026 suspension-expiry decision.

name: Actively Exploited Edge / DevOps / AI-Infra CVEs
status: Cisco Talos publicly attributed active exploitation of Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (CVE-2026-20079, CVSS 10.0, plus companion CVE-2026-20316) to three clusters: JSP-web-shell credential harvesting; a cluster chaining both CVEs with a Cyclops Blink malware variant assessed high-confidence to overlap with Russian GRU-linked Sandworm tooling; and a cluster assessed high-confidence as a Qilin ransomware affiliate. Roughly 700 FMC instances remain internet-exposed. Separately, CISA added a maximum-severity (CVSS 10.0) unauthenticated path-traversal flaw in GitLab CE/EE (CVE-2026-85706) to KEV on 11 Sep; watchTowr observed in-the-wild exploitation within a day of disclosure. Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2026-19490) exploitation continues past its 12 Sep federal deadline without new attribution.
importance: Critical — confirmed simultaneous state-actor and top-tier-ransomware exploitation of DIB-relevant perimeter infrastructure, now joined by a maximum-severity DevOps/software-supply-chain flaw exploited within a day of disclosure.
assessment: This has moved decisively from 'actively exploited, patch now' to 'confirmed named-actor footholds in the wild.' The combination of a Russian state-linked cluster and a major ransomware affiliate exploiting the same flaw, plus near-zero dwell time on the new GitLab CVE, indicates DIB-relevant perimeter and DevOps infrastructure should now be treated as presumed-targeted, not merely vulnerable.
lastChange: 2026-09-14 — Cisco Talos attribution (Sandworm-linked and Qilin-ransomware clusters) on Cisco FMC; new GitLab CVE-2026-85706 KEV addition and rapid exploitation.
orgRelevance: Treat any internet-facing Cisco FMC as potentially compromised and hunt using Talos's published IOCs, not just patch status; patch self-hosted GitLab CE/EE to 19.1.8/19.2.6/19.3.2+ immediately; confirm Citrix NetScaler remediation.
nextIndicator: Confirmed DIB-sector or federal-contractor victim disclosure tied to any FMC cluster; further KEV adds in the DevOps/software-supply-chain category; any new Citrix NetScaler attribution.

name: Golden Dome Procurement
status: ~$1.75B for 36 SDA tracking satellites + up to $3.2B in space-based-interceptor awards; SHIELD IDIQ active; SDA's Tranche 1 Transport Layer A launch (21 Northrop-built satellites) remains scheduled 30 Sep from Vandenberg. The Army has moved to divest its IFPC-High Energy Laser ('Valkyrie,' ~300kW) fielding candidate, redirecting toward the Navy-led E-HEL program feeding Golden Dome's Joint Laser Warfighting System, with prototype delivery reported in the Sep-Oct 2026 timeframe.
importance: High — multi-year homeland-missile-defense demand base, now also consolidating adjacent directed-energy programs.
assessment: Transitioned from funding to procurement; incumbents on SDA/MDA vehicles advantaged. The Army-to-Navy laser-program redirection suggests DoD is converging separate service directed-energy efforts into the Golden Dome architecture rather than sustaining parallel tracks — a structural-consolidation trend worth watching for further mergers.
lastChange: 2026-09-14 — no new award this cycle; Army's Valkyrie high-energy-laser program redirected into the Navy-led E-HEL effort feeding Golden Dome's Joint Laser Warfighting System.
orgRelevance: Assess positioning on SDA/MDA vehicles; firms with legacy Army high-energy-laser involvement should assess transition risk; firms on the Navy-led E-HEL effort may see expanded scope.

name: Ukraine Ceasefire Diplomacy / Zaporizhzhia
status: ZNPP remains on stable, restored external power with no new outage. On 13 Sep, Russia struck the Yahodyn Ukraine-Poland border crossing, which ISW assesses may have been intended to target departing European officials; massed drone/Banderol barrages (453 and 323 drones on successive days) continued alongside continued Ukrainian long-range strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. The narrower 30-day energy-infrastructure strike-halt commitment remains unconfirmed as violated by a grid-specific strike.
importance: High — shapes European security and munitions/air-defense demand; the ZNPP dimension carries independent nuclear-safety significance.
assessment: The war's targeting geography keeps expanding into new categories (border crossings, cross-border airspace) even as the two narrowly-defined pause questions (capital-strike, energy-halt) remain in their previously reported (lapsed/unresolved) states. Witkoff/Kushner-mediated talks reportedly continue with the sides 'getting closer' per US officials, while the Kremlin maintains maximalist terms — continuity language, not a new development.
lastChange: 2026-09-14 — 13 Sep Yahodyn border-crossing strike assessed by ISW as possibly targeting departing European officials; continued massed drone barrages; energy-halt question remains unresolved.
orgRelevance: Macro A&D demand context; no direct organizational action absent personnel travel near the Ukraine-Poland border corridor. ZNPP resolution and the expanding strike-geography pattern remain relevant to critical-infrastructure and airspace-security monitoring.
nextIndicator: A confirmed strike specifically on Ukrainian power/grid infrastructure; any further border-crossing or airspace-incursion incident; movement in the Witkoff/Kushner-mediated talks.

name: Identity-Verification Supply Chain Breach (IDScan.net)
status: IDScan.net (New Orleans-based identity-verification vendor) confirmed on 4 Sep that its cloud platform was breached, consistent with the 'Nexus' dark-web marketplace listing of 153-170M driver's-license/identity-document scans first reported by Brian Krebs on 1 Sep. Over a dozen class-action lawsuits (negligence, breach of implied contract, breach of fiduciary duty, fraud/unjust enrichment) had been filed as of 10 Sep, up from four the prior week; the FBI investigation continues; no FTC or state-AG enforcement action has been publicly confirmed.
importance: High — resolves a prior gap (vendor unconfirmed) and confirms a systemic identity-verification supply-chain compromise with active, growing litigation and unresolved downstream-fraud exposure.
assessment: A confirmed, named, and now heavily litigated breach at a shared identity-verification dependency. The scale (150M+ records) and the document type (government-issued ID scans) make this a systemic fraud-enablement event across any sector relying on document-based identity proofing, not a contained single-vendor incident.
lastChange: 2026-09-14 — thread formalized in continuity tracking on vendor confirmation and mounting litigation (previously tracked only within daily cyber-section items as an open/unconfirmed item).
orgRelevance: Directly confirm whether the organization or its KYC/onboarding vendors use IDScan.net; review contractual indemnification and breach-notification obligations; reinforce identity-proofing fallback and phishing-resistant MFA given the scale of exposed government-ID data.
nextIndicator: Consolidation of the class actions (e.g., an MDL); any FTC or state-AG enforcement action; confirmed downstream fraud incidents traceable to the exposed data.
